A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and all supplied pages, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, neither includes the repeatedly referenced appendices or supplementary material; both end with references. Supplementary sampling details, latency analyses and examples therefore cannot be compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on visual thinking, token usage and visual sensitivity, plus decoding results on MMMU and five additional benchmarks in Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports budget-matched evaluation, component ablations and InternVL transfer results.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same visual perplexity probe, offline phrase mining, uncertainty-triggered lookback insertion and optional branch selection by visual helpfulness. Added implementation explanations and ablation variants do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMMU val, MMBench, MMStar, MathVista, MathVision and MathVerse. The new InternVL evaluations reuse retained tasks and datasets; they extend model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Original Thinking, DEER, DeepConf and REFRAIN remain unchanged in Table 3. Section 4.5 additionally compares the proposed controller against periodic lookback insertion and uncertainty-only branching as ablation controls.

E3.justification: v3 reports an additional fairness control truncating Thinking to the same 16,384-token cap as Instruct, while retaining the original 32,768-token Thinking setting. It also introduces periodic-insertion settings n=1–5, a branching-only control and controller evaluations on InternVL3.5-Think at 4B and 8B.

E4.justification: v3 adds targeted tests of adaptive versus periodic insertion, branching without lookback prompts, budget matching and controller transfer across model families. Existing category, capacity, token-use and visual-sensitivity analyses remain. The explicit observation of similar phrase-alignment patterns across five additional datasets is removed.

E5.justification: The supplied material retains ten sampled paths per item, variation of random seeds, and identical standard-deviation bands and boxplots. No changed run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in all four tables and the seven figure images are unchanged. v3 adds periodic-insertion scores, qualitative budget-matching and branching-only findings, and InternVL MMMU/MMStar gains of +1.5/+1.2 at 4B and +3.3/+3.1 at 8B. Section 4.1 replaces the 89% phrase-alignment result with unquantified 'high alignment' and removes the cross-dataset alignment finding.

T1.justification: The perplexity definition, visual-content and presence contrasts, insertion rule and branch-scoring equation are mathematically unchanged. Moving the perplexity formula inline, renumbering equations and replacing the injection symbol with the established lookback symbol are presentation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract and three stated contributions retain the same central claims: systematic analysis of visual thinking, capacity-dependent token economy, and a training-free controller improving accuracy and efficiency across six benchmarks. The added transfer evidence supports the existing generality claim rather than introducing a new contribution.

C2.justification: v3 restricts the token-economy interpretation to differing vision stacks under a fixed LLM family and adds a limitation for closed-source models without log-probability access. It removes the interpretation that phrase patterns reflect intrinsic LLM behavior rather than dataset artifacts, and adds explanations about insertion disrupting semantic continuity and branching alone failing to restore grounding.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies use of one official InternVL reasoning prompt without averaging alternative prompts, clarifies that tabled baselines use Thinking variants of the same checkpoints, and explicitly states the log-probability access requirement. Conversely, it removes the MathVista-mini, MathVision-full and MathVerse-mini subset identifiers without establishing that the evaluated subsets changed.

R1.justification: v3 removes the 'Reasoning in LLMs' subsection and associated discussion and citations on overthinking, faithfulness, hallucination cues and distribution shifts, including MME-CoT. The main positioning around visual reasoning and adaptive decoding remains. Consolidation and metadata corrections for retained references are bibliographic editing rather than new research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammatical and terminology corrections, shortens parts of the introduction, reduces related work from three subsections to two, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: All seven figures and four tables are retained. The failure example moves from v1 Figure 4 on page 4 to v3 Figure 2 on page 3, and Figure 7 moves from page 7 to page 6. Table 4 is enlarged and its caption completed; equations and surrounding text are also reformatted.

improvement.justification: The added controls, InternVL transfer results and clearer applicability limits are useful, but their evidential benefit is uncertain. The new ablation claims periodic insertion is consistently worse although its InternVL score of 60.4 exceeds the reported 59.2 for the proposed method. Its Qwen reference scores, 59.3/61.6, match Table 3's Design column rather than overall 67.0/69.7, without explaining different settings. Missing supplementary details and removed subset identifiers further prevent a reliable judgment that these additions outweigh the reporting problems.
